evidence.text: Heavy reliance on marketplaces and paid channels early.

A brand with category and offline expansion could compound, but established jewellers are going digital and no moat is described.

evidence.text: Competition from established jewellers going digital.

criteria.rationale: D2C jewellery is squarely a consumer brand.

criteria.rationale: Founder-market fit, earned secrets and build record cannot be assessed: the dossier holds no founder information. The dossier carries no information on how the founders think about or manage this; not inferred from the company description.
Online-first fine silver is a less-crowded entry point with ambition into gold and lab-grown diamonds, but jewellery D2C is not non-consensus overall.

evidence.text: Online-first fine silver jewellery brand, expanding into gold and lab-grown diamonds.

case_for: Squarely a consumer brand with a working online channel and offline expansion (S1, R4).
Category expansion from silver into gold and lab-grown diamonds shows ambition (S4).
case_against: No repeat/cohort data; early growth leaned on marketplaces and paid channels (R3).
Inventory and working-capital intensity strain a pre-seed cheque (R5).
Established jewellers going digital threaten the position (R6).
Early round on a revenue-generating brand may be beyond the fund's lead cheque (S2).
call_questions: What share of customers buy a second time within 6 and 12 months, by acquisition channel?
What share of orders come from paid channels and marketplaces today, and how has it moved?
How many days of inventory do you carry and how is it financed?
What stops a large established jeweller from launching a silver line online and outspending you?
Paid dependence is the weakest part of this story to us: show us the data that says otherwise.
what_would_change_our_view: Cohort repeat data showing a rising share of organic, repeat orders and a working-capital plan that fits the cheque would change our view.
